subject: general
question: A shopkeeper offers a scheme discount of 'Buy goods worth ₹6000 and get ₹1000 worth of goods free'. What is the effective discount percentage (rounded off to two decimals)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **Buy-Free** schemes, the **Effective Discount%** is calculated on the **Total Value** of goods handed over.

Discount% = (Value of Free Goods ÷ Total Value of Goods) × 100

Here, Free Goods = ₹1000 and Paid Goods = ₹6000.

Total Value = 6000 + 1000 = ₹7000.

Discount% = (1000 ÷ 7000) × 100 = 100 ÷ 7 = 14.2857%.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.29%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Formulas → SVG → Steps (⇒ each) → Final Answer.
Formulas: Discount% = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 | MP = Price of all goods (Paid + Free).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6214b09738a00cdd41866358d80aa903489ec1bee95633d2413de322f4903457.png] 
⇒ The **Marked Price (MP)** is the sum of the value of the paid goods and the free goods.
⇒ **MP** = 6000 + 1000 = ₹7000.
⇒ The **Selling Price (SP)** is the actual amount paid by the customer.
⇒ **SP** = ₹6000.
⇒ **Discount** = MP − SP = 7000 − 6000 = ₹1000.
⇒ **Discount%** = (1000 ÷ 7000) × 100 = 14.285...% ≈ 14.29%.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.29%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Discount in "Buy X Get Y Free"

The formula is **Discount% = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100**. Here Y represents the free items and (X+Y) represents the total items.

Marked Price Concept

In any free-item scheme, the shopkeeper incurs the cost of all items, so the total **Marked Price** must include the value of the free items.
